questions.prompt: A company submits a proposed means of compliance for Category 2. It describes the test conditions and methods but omits how the procedure demonstrates that the aircraft satisfies §107.120(a). Which addition addresses that omission?

choices.A: Add the names of pilots who intend to buy the aircraft.
choices.B: Explain how applying the proposed means fulfills the relevant Category 2 requirements.
choices.C: Provide a shipping receipt for the prototype.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: Section 107.155 requires both a description of the procedures and an explanation of how application of the means fulfills the requirements.
Why A is incorrect: Customer names do not explain how the method demonstrates compliance.
Why C is incorrect: Shipment records do not establish the regulatory link between the method and the criteria.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.155 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.155

questions.prompt: A sheltered field reports light winds. A reliable forecast indicates a much stronger wind near the altitude of an exposed ridge the drone must survey. What should the pilot assess before accepting the mission?

choices.A: Whether the surface report and forecast have matching wind directions, regardless of speeds.
choices.B: Only whether the sheltered field stays within limits at takeoff.
choices.C: Whether conditions along the exposed ridge and the return route stay within the aircraft and crew limits.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Launch conditions can be different from conditions at the operating altitude or on the return. Evaluate the actual route and its exposure.
Why A is incorrect: Matching direction does not show that wind speeds are acceptable.
Why B is incorrect: A favorable launch site does not establish safe wind conditions along the route.
Reference: FAA-H-8083-28B, Aviation Weather Handbook — https://www.faa.gov/regulationspolicies/handbooksmanuals/aviation/faa-h-8083-28b-aviation-weather-handbook
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, ch. 11, Aircraft Performance — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak

questions.prompt: A surface weather chart shows a solid red line with semicircles on one side. What is that symbol?

choices.A: A cold front, with the semicircles marking cold air moving behind it.
choices.B: An isobar marking equal surface pressure.
choices.C: A warm front, with the semicircles on the side toward which it is moving.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: A warm front is shown with red semicircles on the side of its advance.
Why A is incorrect: A cold front uses blue triangles.
Why B is incorrect: Isobars connect equal pressure and do not use this frontal symbol.
Reference: FAA-H-8083-28B, Aviation Weather Handbook — https://www.faa.gov/regulationspolicies/handbooksmanuals/aviation/faa-h-8083-28b-aviation-weather-handbook

questions.prompt: A drone takes off at 0.54 pound for a Category 1 flight over people. During a preliminary spray-system test, a collector on the aircraft will accumulate 0.03 pound of water and retain it for the remainder of the operation. What should the pilot change before using this plan under Category 1?

choices.A: Use the setup because Category 1 weight is measured only at takeoff.
choices.B: Use the setup because material collected in flight is excluded from the aircraft weight.
choices.C: Prevent the aircraft from exceeding 0.55 pound throughout the operation or use another lawful plan.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Once collected, the water is onboard and the total would be 0.57 pound. The limit applies throughout the operation.
Why A is incorrect: Passing the takeoff check does not allow exceeding the limit later.
Why B is incorrect: The weight of material carried onboard counts.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.110 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.110

questions.prompt:
Written scenario data: The flight-briefing table gives time separations from a crewed aircraft's estimated crossing: Option West 42 seconds, Option East 25 seconds, Option South 15 seconds.

The written scenario data provide three proposed drone crossing times and one estimated aircraft crossing time at the same point. The crew's briefing requires a planned separation of at least 30 seconds. Based on the estimates alone, which drone option meets that minimum?

choices.A: Option West only.
choices.B: Option East only.
choices.C: Option South only.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: Option West is 42 seconds away from the aircraft estimate, so it meets the planning criterion. Actual traffic must still be observed and yielded to as required.
Why B is incorrect: Option East differs by only 25 seconds. The estimate does not provide the specified margin.
Why C is incorrect: Option South differs from the aircraft estimate by only 15 seconds.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chs. 2 and 17, Decision-Making and Aeromedical Factors — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: FAA AIM, §4-2, Radio Communications Phraseology and Techniques — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap4_section_2.html
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.37 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.37

questions.prompt: A standard Remote ID aircraft stops broadcasting in flight. Directly beneath it is an occupied patio. A clear recovery spot is immediately to one side. The control link still works. What action satisfies the Part 89 failure response?

choices.A: Descend straight onto the patio because the aircraft must land instantly at its current position.
choices.B: Use the clear recovery spot and land as soon as practicable.
choices.C: Continue the mission because the command link still works.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The person at the controls must land as soon as practicable after the required broadcast stops. The adjacent safe spot addresses that requirement.
Why A is incorrect: The rule does not require choosing an unsafe point when prompt safe recovery is available.
Why C is incorrect: A working command link does not restore the required broadcast.
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.110 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89/section-89.110
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf

questions.prompt: A customer wants to request a Part 107 waiver specifically to carry a package confirmed to be hazardous material. The customer proposes an upgraded container and extensive safety testing. Is §107.36 eligible for relief through the Part 107 waiver list?

choices.A: No. Section 107.36 is outside the list of provisions that can be waived under §107.205.
choices.B: Yes. The Part 107 groundspeed waiver also waives the cargo restriction.
choices.C: Yes. Listing stronger containment makes §107.36 eligible for a Part 107 waiver.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: The Part 107 waiver list does not include the hazardous-material carriage rule.
Why B is incorrect: Relief from a groundspeed limit does not provide relief from the separate cargo rule.
Why C is incorrect: Mitigation does not add a rule to the list of waivable provisions.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.36 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.36
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.205 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.205
Reference: 49 CFR § 171.8, Hazardous material definition — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-B/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-171/section-171.8

questions.prompt: A Category 4 operator proposes using a substitute part that physically fits but is known to leave the aircraft in a worse condition than its original or properly altered condition. Can the responsible person use it as proposed?

choices.A: Yes. The substitute is allowed if the maintenance entry identifies its lower quality.
choices.B: Yes. Physical fit alone satisfies the part-quality requirement.
choices.C: No. The applicable part-quality requirement calls for a condition at least equal to the original or properly altered condition.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The Category 4 maintenance provision addresses resulting aircraft condition, rather than fit alone.
Why A is incorrect: Documentation does not cure a failure to meet the parts requirement.
Why B is incorrect: Fit does not show equivalent condition.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.140 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.140

questions.prompt: An airport data block shows the FAA weather-camera symbol. A crew wants to check visibility along a survey several miles away. How should it use the symbol?

choices.A: Locate the camera imagery as one observation source and verify current visibility at the control station.
choices.B: Use the symbol as proof that the entire survey area has at least three statute miles of visibility.
choices.C: Treat the camera listing as the airport's controlled-airspace authorization.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: The symbol identifies access to weather imagery. The actual route and control station still need an assessment.
Why B is incorrect: The presence of a camera does not establish a visibility value.
Why C is incorrect: Weather imagery is not an ATC authorization.

questions.prompt: A new crew member is designated as visual observer. Which task belongs to that role during flight?

choices.A: Serve as the camera operator and review image quality throughout every pass.
choices.B: Assist the pilot and control operator in seeing and avoiding aircraft and other hazards.
choices.C: Approve the flight plan on behalf of ATC.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The visual observer assists with seeing and avoiding other aircraft and objects aloft or on the ground.
Why A is incorrect: A camera-quality assignment is not the visual observer's defining task and may interfere with observation.
Why C is incorrect: The observer cannot issue an ATC authorization.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.3 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.3
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.33 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.33

questions.prompt: Near a mirrored building facade, the observer can see both the actual drone and a reflection that appears to move in the opposite direction. What should the crew do before continuing close work?

choices.A: Average the positions of the aircraft and the reflection.
choices.B: Follow the reflection because it is brighter than the aircraft.
choices.C: Maintain a safe standoff and reposition if needed to keep an unambiguous direct view.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The crew needs a reliable direct reference for separation. A safe pause and viewing change can remove the ambiguity.
Why A is incorrect: A midpoint between the aircraft and its reflection has no operational basis.
Why B is incorrect: A brighter reflected image is not the aircraft's real position.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chs. 2 and 17, Decision-Making and Aeromedical Factors — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf

questions.prompt: An observer reports a low aircraft on a converging path but cannot identify the type. The pilot can stop the drone's approach to the shared area. What should happen first?

choices.A: Continue because the report lacks an aircraft registration number.
choices.B: Stay clear and use the reported position and movement to manage the possible conflict.
choices.C: Continue until the observer identifies the aircraft make and model.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The reported path indicates a potential conflict regardless of the aircraft's identity. Prioritize separation and yielding.
Why A is incorrect: The registration number is not needed to recognize the immediate traffic hazard.
Why C is incorrect: The make and model are not prerequisites for acting on the conflict.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chs. 2 and 17, Decision-Making and Aeromedical Factors — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.37 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.37
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf

questions.prompt: A Part 61 private pilot is also a remote pilot. The pilot completed a current flight review but has no qualifying Part 107 test or training within the applicable recency period. Which action can the pilot take on the Part 61-based route?

choices.A: Renew aircraft registration and use it as proof of pilot recency.
choices.B: Treat the flight review alone as the required Part 107 training.
choices.C: Complete the qualifying training covering the knowledge areas in §107.74.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The Part 61-based route requires both meeting the flight review requirements and completing the applicable training.
Why A is incorrect: Registration has no bearing on the remote pilot's knowledge recency.
Why B is incorrect: A flight review does not by itself complete the Part 107 knowledge requirement.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.65 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.65
Reference: FAA, Become a Certificated Remote Pilot — https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/become_a_drone_pilot

questions.prompt:
Written scenario data: Training configurations list total aircraft weight and wing area: Quartz 8.8 lb and 5.5 sq ft; Slate 8.4 lb and 5.0 sq ft; Copper 9.0 lb and 5.4 sq ft.

The written scenario data list three fixed-wing training configurations. For this exercise the manufacturer's wing-loading limit is 1.60 pounds per square foot, and all other limits are met. Divide loaded weight by wing area. Which configuration meets the wing-loading limit?

choices.A: Configuration Slate only.
choices.B: Configuration Quartz only.
choices.C: Configuration Copper only.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: Quartz has 8.8 ÷ 5.5 = 1.60 pounds per square foot, which meets the limit.
Why A is incorrect: Slate has 8.4 ÷ 5.0 = 1.68 pounds per square foot, above the limit.
Why C is incorrect: Copper has 9.0 ÷ 5.4, about 1.67 pounds per square foot, above the limit.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, ch. 5, Aerodynamics of Flight — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, ch. 11, Aircraft Performance — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak

questions.prompt: A remote pilot wants to show the chief pilot that the FAA recurrent training was completed. Which record is relevant to that check?

choices.A: The FAA course completion certificate with the pilot's name and completion date.
choices.B: A receipt for the aircraft's registration fee.
choices.C: The company's proof of insurance for the job.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: The course completion certificate documents the training event used for knowledge recency.
Why B is incorrect: Aircraft registration does not document a pilot's training.
Why C is incorrect: Insurance addresses coverage, rather than when the FAA course was completed.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.65 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.65
Reference: FAA, Become a Certificated Remote Pilot — https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/become_a_drone_pilot

questions.prompt: A UAG-style form includes 60 scored questions and five unscored validation questions. A student answers 41 scored questions correctly and gets all five validation questions right. Does the student reach the 70 percent threshold?

choices.A: Yes. Add the five validation answers to get 46 correct scored items.
choices.B: No. The student has 41 out of 60 scored items and needs 42.
choices.C: Yes. Divide 46 by 65 to determine the official scored result.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The threshold is 42 correct out of the 60 scored items. Validation answers do not contribute to the score.
Why A is incorrect: Correct validation responses are still unscored.
Why C is incorrect: The calculation includes unscored items in both the numerator and denominator.
Reference: PSI UAG Applicant Information Bulletin, effective September 29, 2025, p. 4 — https://media.psiexams.com/faa/UAG_Information_Bulletin.pdf#page=4
Reference: FAA Airman Knowledge Testing Matrix, revision September 25, 2026, pp. 2 and 15 — https://www.faa.gov/training_testing/testing/testing_matrix

questions.prompt: The FAA determines that an emergency related to safety exists for an aircraft covered by an accepted Category 2 declaration. The declaration holder says the FAA must always start the ordinary proposed-rescission process before acting. What does §107.160 provide in this situation?

choices.A: The FAA must wait for the next routine inspection regardless of the emergency.
choices.B: Only the local remote PIC can rescind a declaration in a safety emergency.
choices.C: The FAA may issue an emergency rescission order without first starting the ordinary process in §107.160(d)(3).

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The emergency provision allows an immediate order under the stated statutory authority without beginning the ordinary notice process.
Why A is incorrect: The special provision exists to address a safety emergency without waiting for the ordinary process.
Why B is incorrect: The FAA, rather than an individual operator, takes the rescission action.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.160 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.160

questions.prompt: An applicable notice restricts a defined area from the surface through 250 feet AGL between 1400Z and 1500Z. The route lies inside the lateral limits. It will be at 280 feet AGL at 1405Z and later at 220 feet AGL at 1430Z. Assume all other applicable rules are met. Which planned point is inside this restriction?

choices.A: The 1430Z point only.
choices.B: The 1405Z point only.
choices.C: Both points because both times fall inside the window.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: Both times are in the stated window, but only the 220-foot point falls within the restricted altitude band.
Why B is incorrect: The 280-foot point is above the stated restriction ceiling.
Why C is incorrect: The time test alone does not determine whether a point falls in the restricted volume.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.47 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.47
Reference: FAA, Temporary Flight Restrictions — https://tfr.faa.gov/tfr3/
Reference: FAA AIM, §5-1-3, Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) System — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap5_section_1.html

questions.prompt:
Written scenario data: The left-to-right neutral-position differences are: Setup A 1 degree, Setup B 3 degrees, Setup C 2 degrees. Maximum permitted difference is 2 degrees inclusive.

The manual allows a left-to-right neutral-position difference of no more than 2 degrees. Which listed setup fails that check?

choices.A: Setup B only.
choices.B: Setup C only.
choices.C: Setup A only.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: Setup B differs by 3 degrees between the two sides.
Why B is incorrect: Setup C differs by exactly 2 degrees, which meets the stated maximum.
Why C is incorrect: Setup A differs by 1 degree and is within tolerance.
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.15 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.15

questions.prompt: A new antenna doubles usable command range. The planned extended segment would be too far away for any crewmember to determine the drone's attitude and direction with unaided vision. What should the crew do for an ordinary VLOS flight?

choices.A: Use the drone's video feed alone in the extended segment.
choices.B: Use the full antenna range because a stronger link expands the legal visual range.
choices.C: Shorten or redesign the route so the crew can meet the visual requirements.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The command link and visual capability serve different requirements. The extended segment does not meet the visual condition.
Why A is incorrect: Camera video is not a substitute for the stated visual ability.
Why B is incorrect: Signal range does not determine VLOS.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.31 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.31
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf

questions.prompt:
Written scenario data: The chart note at Stone Mountain reads that there is a magnetic disturbance of 10 degrees and includes an associated elevation; it does not give ATC authorization or a fixed radius.

What issue is specifically identified in the Stone Mountain note in the written scenario data?

choices.A: A requirement to fly magnetic course 010 degrees below 4,000 feet.
choices.B: A 10-nautical-mile circle where ordinary compass headings replace ATC authorization.
choices.C: A local magnetic disturbance of as much as 10 degrees at 4,000 feet elevation.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The printed note describes a magnetic disturbance and gives an amount and elevation. It does not predict a precise error for every aircraft or location.
Why A is incorrect: The 10-degree value describes a disturbance, not a mandated heading.
Why B is incorrect: The note does not define a radius or grant ATC authorization.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, July 9, 2026, VFR Terms and Symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/

questions.prompt: An owner plans to register one small unmanned aircraft under Part 47 instead of Part 48. The owner asks whether §48.1(b) requires both sets of federal registration and marking rules simultaneously. How is that provision structured?

choices.A: It lets the pilot use a Part 107 certificate in place of both registration options.
choices.B: It always requires both Part 47 and Part 48 registrations for a work drone.
choices.C: It offers either the Part 48 route or the applicable Part 47 registration with Part 45 markings.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Section 48.1(b) sets out alternative registration and marking routes, subject to applicable exceptions.
Why A is incorrect: The operator's credential does not replace the aircraft's registration.
Why B is incorrect: The alternatives are not both required by that provision.

questions.prompt: Two valid flight authorizations cover adjoining portions of a route over level ground at 620 feet MSL. One limits the flight to 140 feet AGL, and the other limits it to 735 feet MSL. The crew wants one altitude above the ground for the entire route. What is the highest listed option that meets both?

choices.A: 140 feet AGL.
choices.B: 115 feet AGL.
choices.C: 130 feet AGL.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The second ceiling is 115 feet AGL after subtracting the ground elevation from 735 feet MSL. It is more restrictive than 140 feet AGL.
Why A is incorrect: 140 feet AGL would be 760 feet MSL, above the second ceiling.
Why C is incorrect: 130 feet AGL would be 750 feet MSL, above the second ceiling.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.41 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.41

questions.prompt: A venue crew begins raising a suspended banner through the drone's planned path. The banner is moving and its final position is not yet known. The aircraft has a safe holding point clear of the work. What should the pilot do?

choices.A: Hold clear and verify the final obstruction position before approving any revised route.
choices.B: Follow the original path because the last survey map did not show the raised banner.
choices.C: Fly through the area faster so the banner has less time to move.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: The obstruction is changing. A safe hold gives the crew time to confirm actual clearance.
Why B is incorrect: A previously accurate map can be outdated when the site changes.
Why C is incorrect: Speed does not make an uncertain obstacle position safe.

Which named facility is associated with channel 105 and the identifier GQO?

choices.A: Choo Choo.

choices.C: Daisy.

questions.prompt: The Category 2 label is damaged. The pilot makes a correct English replacement, but plans to hold it beside the drone for a launch photo instead of attaching it. What must change before operations over people?

choices.A: Attach the label to the carrying case rather than the aircraft.
choices.B: Keep the photo because showing the label once satisfies the display requirement.
choices.C: Attach a legible, prominent label that will remain on the aircraft for the duration of the operation.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Section 107.135 requires a correct English label that remains on the aircraft throughout the operation.
Why A is incorrect: The carrying case does not accompany the aircraft in flight.
Why B is incorrect: A one-time image does not meet the continued aircraft-labeling condition.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.135 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.135

questions.prompt: A drone flies at a warehouse site. The remote PIC argues that customers on the ground are solely the property owner's concern. Who has the Part 107 duty to ensure the operation will pose no undue hazard to people if control is lost?

choices.A: The property owner instead of the remote pilot in command.
choices.B: The aircraft registration office.
choices.C: The remote pilot in command.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Section 107.19 assigns this flight-safety duty to the remote PIC.
Why A is incorrect: The property owner can help manage the site, but the duty under this section remains with the remote PIC.
Why B is incorrect: Registration staff do not direct or assess the site operation.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.19 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.19

questions.prompt: A camera operator asks the visual observer to review a replay on a tablet while the aircraft holds near a public access route. The observer is the only person assigned to scan the approach sector. What should the crew do?

choices.A: Review the replay immediately because a hover eliminates the need to monitor the approach.
choices.B: Keep the observer on the live scan and review the replay after landing or after coverage has been properly reassigned.
choices.C: Alternate every few seconds without letting the remote PIC know the observer is looking away.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The held aircraft still needs a reliable traffic and hazard scan. Replay review should not displace the assigned live task.
Why A is incorrect: Hovering does not prevent traffic or people from approaching.
Why C is incorrect: An unannounced split can create a coverage gap the pilot does not anticipate.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chs. 2 and 17, Decision-Making and Aeromedical Factors — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf

questions.prompt: A remote PIC and the person manipulating the controls remain at a fixed station. A designated visual observer rides in a slow vehicle, with effective communications and the required visual capability throughout. Considering only §107.25, does the observer's movement by itself mean the pilot is operating the aircraft from a moving land vehicle?

choices.A: Yes. The drone must be considered operated from the vehicle whenever the observer reports traffic.
choices.B: No. The people operating the aircraft from the control station remain at a fixed location.
choices.C: Yes. Any vehicle used by any crewmember makes the flight one operated from that vehicle.

questions.explanation:
Why B works: The moving-platform restriction concerns operating the aircraft from the moving vehicle. The scenario keeps the actual controls and remote PIC at the fixed station.
Why A is incorrect: A traffic report does not move the control station.

questions.prompt: After takeoff, a fixed-wing drone has 18 seconds to climb before reaching a low obstacle. questions.prompt: An airport symbol depicts two paved runways. A crew needs to know which runway may have aircraft traffic during the survey. Which information is most useful alongside the symbol?

choices.A: Only the total number of airspace shelves shown around the airport.
choices.B: The airport symbol alone, because both runways must be active whenever two are drawn.
choices.C: Current runway status and operating information, including applicable notices and current airport procedures.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: The symbol conveys physical charted information. Status and traffic use need current operational information.
Why A is incorrect: Shelf count does not show current runway status.
Why B is incorrect: Depicted pavement does not prove both runways are currently usable.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, July 9, 2026, VFR Terms and Symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/
Reference: FAA, Digital Chart Supplement — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/dafd/
Reference: FAA AIM, §5-1-3, Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) System — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap5_section_1.html

questions.prompt: A Part 48-registered standard Remote ID drone broadcasts correctly. Its external FAA aircraft identifier has been removed. Does the working broadcast satisfy Part 48's marking requirement by itself?

choices.A: Yes. A working radio broadcast satisfies the physical marking rule.
choices.B: Yes. Marking applies only when a drone has no electronics.
choices.C: No. Restore the required identifier on a legible external surface before operating.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Remote ID and the Part 48 external identifier serve separate requirements.
Why A is incorrect: An electronic transmission does not put a legible identifier on the aircraft.
Why B is incorrect: The marking requirement is not limited to aircraft without electronics.
Reference: 14 CFR § 48.200 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-48/section-48.200
Reference: 14 CFR § 48.205 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-48/section-48.205
Reference: 14 CFR § 89.110 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-89/section-89.110

questions.prompt: A crew member reports an obstacle as “90 feet,” but cannot remember whether the site note lists height above ground or elevation above sea level. The drone is approaching on a tight clearance plan. What should the pilot do?

choices.A: Pause the approach safely and verify the obstacle's reference before continuing.
choices.B: Average the possible interpretations and use that as the clearance estimate.
choices.C: Assume the number is above ground because the crew is flying a drone.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: A value without a confirmed reference cannot support a tight clearance judgment. Verify the datum or use a route that safely avoids the uncertainty.
Why B is incorrect: Averaging incompatible interpretations does not establish the real obstruction height.
Why C is incorrect: The type of aircraft does not determine how the obstacle was described.
Reference: FAA AIM, §4-2, Radio Communications Phraseology and Techniques — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap4_section_2.html
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chs. 2 and 17, Decision-Making and Aeromedical Factors — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf

questions.prompt: A cropped chart shows the label of an alert area but cuts off the supporting information about its vertical limits and activity. What should the briefing include before assessing a flight near it?

choices.A: Treat the label as proof that the area extends from the surface to unlimited altitude.
choices.B: Treat the missing details as proof that the area has been canceled.
choices.C: Use the full current chart and applicable airspace information to check the area, activity, and limits.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: A cropped image cannot establish information it excludes. The complete source is needed for the planned flight.
Why A is incorrect: The missing details do not imply an unlimited vertical extent.
Why B is incorrect: The crop does not establish cancellation.
Reference: FAA Aeronautical Chart Users’ Guide, July 9, 2026, VFR Terms and Symbols — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/digital_products/aero_guide/
Reference: FAA AIM, §3-4, Special Use Airspace — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap3_section_4.html

questions.prompt: An existing waiver permits a test at Site A. The operator asks the FAA to add Site B and receives an acknowledgment, but no amended waiver. Can the operator rely on the waiver at Site B today?

choices.A: No. The operator must stay within the issued terms unless an applicable amendment or separate authority is in place.
choices.B: Yes. The operator can replace the FAA-approved site internally if the aircraft is unchanged.
choices.C: Yes. An acknowledgment automatically adds the new site to the issued terms.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: The issued waiver defines its scope. An acknowledged request does not itself extend that scope.
Why B is incorrect: The operator cannot unilaterally change an FAA waiver.
Why C is incorrect: Acknowledging a submission is not approving it.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.200 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.200

questions.prompt: A temporary remote pilot certificate lists an expiration date next month. Today the holder receives a notice that the certificate sought has been denied. What happens to the temporary certificate?

choices.A: It automatically becomes a permanent certificate for the rest of the printed period.
choices.B: It stays valid until the printed expiration date regardless of the notice.
choices.C: It expires upon receipt of the denial notice.

questions.explanation:
Why C works: Receipt of a denial or revocation notice is an independent expiration event for the temporary credential.
Why A is incorrect: A denial notice does not issue a permanent certificate.
Why B is incorrect: The printed date does not override an earlier expiration trigger.
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.64 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.64

questions.prompt: The crew holds the drone clear of a runway approach because an airplane reported final. The airplane then reports a go-around and begins climbing on a different path toward the survey area. What should the pilot do?

choices.A: Keep clear and reassess the airplane's new path before resuming the drone task.
choices.B: Resume as soon as the airplane passes the planned touchdown point because the final approach is finished.
choices.C: Continue because a climbing airplane cannot be a conflict with a low-flying drone.

questions.explanation:
Why A works: A go-around changes the expected traffic path. The crew must use the new movement and keep the drone clear.
Why B is incorrect: The previous touchdown plan is no longer the relevant prediction.
Why C is incorrect: A climb can still cross a low-altitude route before adequate separation exists.
Reference: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, chs. 2 and 17, Decision-Making and Aeromedical Factors — https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/phak
Reference: 14 CFR § 107.37 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-107/section-107.37
Reference: FAA AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft System — https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf
